comparisons.peer_summary: The Company has four reportable segments: Data Center (including AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, etc.), Client (CPUs, APUs, chipsets for desktops/notebooks), Gaming (discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoCs), and Embedded (embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, SOMs).
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD explicitly define their reportable business segments in Item 8. AVGO divides its business into two broad segments: Semiconductor Solutions and Infrastructure Software. In contrast, AMD structures its business into four specific reportable segments: Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded. While AVGO’s Semiconductor Solutions segment broadly covers data center and networking products (including AI), AMD explicitly details its Data Center segment as including AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, and DPUs, highlighting a more granular segmentation of its semiconductor offerings compared to AVGO's two-segment model.

sentences.text: We have two reportable segments: semiconductor solutions and infrastructure software.
The Company's four reportable segments are:

comparisons.peer_summary: Business is organized into Intel Products, Intel Foundry, and All other; CCG, DCAI, and Intel Foundry are reportable operating segments, while NEX, Altera, and Mobileye are non-reportable segments with selective disclosure.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and INTC disclose their reportable operating segments in Item 8. AVGO operates with two reportable segments (Semiconductor Solutions and Infrastructure Software), whereas INTC organizes its business into three primary operating segments (CCG, DCAI, and Intel Foundry) with additional non-reportable segments disclosed selectively. A key difference is that AVGO’s segments are based on product type and market (semiconductors vs. software), while INTC’s DCAI segment specifically mirrors the AI/data center focus seen in AVGO and AMD, but INTC also separates its manufacturing capabilities into the Intel Foundry segment, which is not a separate reportable segment for AVGO.

comparisons.peer_topic: Definition of Compute and Networking Business Unit (CNBU)
comparisons.peer_summary: The Compute and Networking Business Unit includes memory products and solutions sold into the data center, PC, graphics, and networking markets.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU describe their business units/segments in Item 8, though with different scopes. AVGO’s Semiconductor Solutions segment includes products for data center networking and storage (FC SAN). MU explicitly defines its Compute and Networking Business Unit (CNBU) as including memory products sold into the data center, PC, and networking markets. While both companies serve the data center and networking markets, AVGO’s disclosure is broader, encompassing infrastructure software and various semiconductor components, whereas MU’s CNBU is specifically focused on memory solutions within those markets.

sentences.text: We offer thousands of products that are used in end products such as enterprise and data center networking, including artificial intelligence ("AI") networking and connectivity, home connectivity, set-top boxes, broadband access, telecommunication equipment, smartphones and base stations, data center servers and storage systems, factory automation, power generation and alternative energy systems, and electronic displays.
Compute and Networking Business Unit ("CNBU"): Includes memory products and solutions sold into the data center, PC, graphics, and networking markets.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Compute & Networking segment includes the Data Center accelerated computing platform, networking, automotive AI cockpit and autonomous driving solutions, electric vehicle computing platforms, Jetson for robotics, NVIDIA AI Enterprise software, and DGX Cloud.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and NVDA define their reportable segments with a strong emphasis on Data Center and Networking capabilities, reflecting their roles in the AI infrastructure market. AVGO’s Semiconductor Solutions segment includes AI networking and connectivity products, while NVDA’s Compute & Networking segment explicitly includes the Data Center accelerated computing platform and networking. Both companies treat AI networking and data center acceleration as core components of their primary semiconductor segments, although AVGO also maintains a distinct Infrastructure Software segment which NVDA does not report as a separate operating segment in the same manner.

sentences.text: We offer thousands of products that are used in end products such as enterprise and data center networking, including artificial intelligence ("AI") networking and connectivity, home connectivity, set-top boxes, broadband access, telecommunication equipment, smartphones and base stations, data center servers and storage systems, factory automation, power generation and alternative energy systems, and electronic displays.

The Compute & Networking segment includes our Data Center accelerated computing platform; networking; automotive artificial intelligence, or AI, Cockpit, autonomous driving development agreements, and autonomous vehicle solutions; electric vehicle computing platforms; Jetson for robotics and other embedded platforms; NVIDIA AI Enterprise and other software; and DGX Cloud.
